answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, so an identity’s influence depends on reachable, independently supported paths rather than raw key count. A sybil cluster represented by falcon, jetty, and umber, if sparsely connected to honest nodes, has low conductance: few edges cross its boundary relative to its volume. Conductance and min-cut bounds limit walk flow into the cluster, thereby bounding its aggregate voting weight despite internal collusion.
